references.text: Isaiah describes the Lord's sword as saturated with blood and covered in fat, from lambs and rams—an image of God's judgment similar to Deuteronomy 32:42, where God's sword devours flesh.
The Lord will let oppressors eat their own flesh and be drowned by their own blood—a parallel theme of God's vengeful judgment through blood and flesh.
Jeremiah describes how the Lord's sword shall devour and become saturated with blood—a direct parallel to the image of the sword that devours flesh in Deuteronomy.
Ezekiel describes God's great sacrificial feast where birds will eat flesh and drink blood from princes and heroes—the same theme of God's judgment through bloodshed.
Revelation describes the birds called to eat the flesh of kings, commanders, and mighty men—an eschatological fulfillment of the image from Deuteronomy regarding God's vengeful judgment.
The blood flowing from the winepress up to the horses' bridles—an image of God's wrath and judgment corresponding to the arrows that are drunk with blood in Deuteronomy.
Balaam's prophecy about Israel as a lion drinking the blood of the slain—a similar image of victory and judgment over enemies.
